Definition: from a derivative of G2378; a place of sacrifice, i.e. an altar (special or genitive case, literal or figurative):--altar.
BiblicalUsage: thysiastḗrion is the word the Bible uses when it means an altar, a place of sacrifice. In Matthew 5:23, Therefore if thou bring thy gift to the altar. That is the sense it carries through all 21 of its occurrences.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the altar is where sin is dealt with honestly, not hidden. That is why thysiastḗrion stays with me long after the verse is closed.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
